chunks: I asked him about the woman who has istihadha, so he said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) was asked about the woman with istihadha, so he commanded her to wait during the days of her haydh, not praying during them, then to perform ghusl and insert cotton and use a cloth as a belt, then to pray until the blood comes through the cloth. He said: The bleeding woman performs ghusl between every two prayers, and the istidh-far is that she applies perfume and burns incense with dukhnah and other things, and the istithfar is that she fashions something like the breech strap of an animal.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on prayer for a woman experiencing istihadha (inter-period bleeding) according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal ruling (fatwa) transmitted by Imam al-Sadiq (AS) from Imam al-Baqir (AS), who in turn reports from the Prophet (SAWW). The ruling addresses istihadha — the condition of inter-period vaginal bleeding that is not classified as menstruation (haydh). The woman must observe her normal haydh days without prayer, then after ghusl, she inserts cotton, dons a special protective cloth belt, and may continue praying. Between each pair of prayers, she performs ghusl again, and she is instructed to use perfume and incense (istidh-far) and to secure the protective cloth in the manner of an animal's breech strap (istithfar). This ruling reflects the early Islamic jurisprudential tradition of distinguishing ritual states and establishing practical procedures for maintaining ritual purity.
